html:
The Anglo-Kuwaiti Agreement was a secret treaty signed in January 1899 between Sheikh Mubarak Al Sabah of Kuwait and Britain. Mubarak promised not to give land to or receive agents of any other power without British consent.

Mubarak had taken power in 1896 by killing his two half-brothers. He feared both the Ottomans, who counted Kuwait as part of their province of Basra, and the plan of a German Baghdad Railway ending on his coast. Britain wanted to keep rivals off the road to India.

The agreement made Kuwait a British protectorate in all but name. It kept Kuwait outside the Iraq that Britain built after 1920, which is why later Iraqi rulers claimed it, up to the invasion of 1990. Kuwait gained full independence in 1961.
sum: The Anglo-Kuwaiti Agreement was a secret treaty signed in January 1899 between Sheikh Mubarak Al Sabah of Kuwait and Britain. Mubarak promised not to give land to or receive agents of any other power without British consent.
